options.name: Copper Workshop
options.architecture: dark / warm single identity (fills only on brand+primary CTA) / cool-desaturated status tints

status.run: ▶ + word [RUNNING] + inverted row (static equivalent for reduced-motion)

color_independent_signals.selection_focus_unavailable: Selection = inverted fill; focus = outer dashed ring in focus_ring token; unavailable = dashed border + reason line.

options.hierarchy: Copper = brand mark + the one primary CTA per view. Status tints come from a separate cool/desaturated family so copper never reads as 'running' or 'warning'.
options.v1_change: v1 reused copper as `run`; v2 gives run its own steel-blue tint so identity≠status.
options.tradeoff: Warm accent can still read 'warning' next to a salmon blocked tint; blocked is always a filled panel with [BLOCKED] + ✕ + reason line.
options.mono_fallback: Copper→#fff fill, tints→#fff text; ✕ hatch retained; invert selection + dashed focus.
options.source_inspiration: Interpretive of the earlier FTLO Living Factory warm-workshop mood (copper connections); not measured from reference images.

options.name: Heat Ramp Foundry
options.architecture: dark / color encodes QUANTITY (sequential ramp), never state; identity = single salmon rule

status.run: ▶ + word [RUNNING] + inverted row (static equivalent for reduced-motion)

color_independent_signals.selection_focus_unavailable: Selection = inverted fill; focus = outer dashed ring in focus_ring token; unavailable = dashed border + reason line.

options.hierarchy: Ramp is for throughput/load/queue-depth cells only and every cell prints its number; ramp is monotonic in luminance so it survives greyscale. Identity = one salmon rule; status uses separate pastel tints.
options.v1_change: v1 'Lava Foundry' was Copper with a hotter orange (near-duplicate). v2 repurposes the hue family as a data ramp — a different job.
options.tradeoff: Ramp invites reading hot=bad; label as LOAD not HEALTH, and print numerals + hatch density in each cell.
options.source_inspiration: Interpretive of Vulcanus/lava mood and of Factorio heat/production overlays; the ramp itself is a standard sequential-ramp idea, not extracted from a screenshot.

options.name: Deck Cyan Hairline
options.architecture: dark / cool / color lives ONLY in lines, ports, focus (never fills); status is uncolored text

status.run: ▶ + word [RUNNING] + inverted row (static equivalent for reduced-motion)

color_independent_signals.selection_focus_unavailable: Selection = inverted fill; focus = outer dashed ring in focus_ring token; unavailable = dashed border + reason line.

options.hierarchy: Cyan = 1-3px connection lines, port squares, top rule. Status words/glyphs stay text-colored; only BLOCKED gets a (rose-tinted) fill.
options.v1_change: v1 let cyan double as `run`; v2 removes it (status uncolored) so cyan is purely wiring identity.
options.tradeoff: Sterile; relies on typography and spacing. Hairlines at 1px can vanish at low DPI — use 2px minimum for connection lines.
options.mono_fallback: Cyan lines→#fff lines; fills unchanged (already none).
options.source_inspiration: Interpretive of Space-Platform graphite deck + connection lines; not measured.

options.name: Blueprint Paper
options.architecture: light / cool white / blue = REFERENCES only (ids, coordinates, links, focus)

status.run: ▶ + word [RUNNING] + inverted row (static equivalent for reduced-motion)

color_independent_signals.selection_focus_unavailable: Selection = inverted fill; focus = outer dashed ring in focus_ring token; unavailable = dashed border + reason line.

options.hierarchy: Blue marks things you can point at: step ids, schema paths, links, the focus ring. Body and status are ink. Blocked = inverted ink panel.
options.v1_change: v1 painted OK marks blue (traffic-light/identity collision); v2 removes blue from every status.
options.tradeoff: Looks like docs more than an app; add a real surface hierarchy via rules, not tint.
options.source_inspiration: Interpretive of blueprint/plan-sheet convention (coordinates as references); not measured.

options.name: Wire Triad
options.architecture: dark / THREE lane-type hues (blue/violet/sand) each paired with a line pattern; status neutral

status.run: ▶ + word [RUNNING] + inverted row (static equivalent for reduced-motion)

color_independent_signals.selection_focus_unavailable: Selection = inverted fill; focus = outer dashed ring in focus_ring token; unavailable = dashed border + reason line.

options.hierarchy: Lane hues label DECLARED lane kinds (input/transform/output), each also carries a pattern and a 2-letter tag. Focus is white (not a lane hue). Status is neutral glyph+word.
options.v1_change: v1 used green/red/blue — a literal traffic light for identity. v2 removes red/green from identity entirely.
options.tradeoff: Violet vs blue is the weakest pair (see CVD sim); patterns+tags are mandatory not decorative. Violet sits near F17.06 magenta — never combine those.
options.source_inspiration: Interpretive of Factorio circuit-wire identity colours (red/green wires) deliberately NOT copied because red/green collides with status; lanes use blue/violet/sand + patterns.

options.name: Cursor Signal
options.architecture: dark / near-mono / ONE hot hue (magenta) reserved for 'where you are' (focus, cursor, selection pointer)

status.run: ▶ + word [RUNNING] + inverted row (static equivalent for reduced-motion)

color_independent_signals.selection_focus_unavailable: Selection = inverted fill; focus = outer dashed ring in focus_ring token; unavailable = dashed border + reason line.

options.hierarchy: Magenta appears exactly once per screen: the focus/cursor. Everything else is Jaryo ink. Running uses an animated chevron whose reduced-motion form is static [RUN].
options.v1_change: v1 'Ink & Signal' used yellow for BOTH focus and running (collision) and duplicated Hazard's hue; v2 = magenta, focus-only.
options.tradeoff: Almost no brand color; marketing may find it austere. Magenta ring on white panels needs ≥3:1 (checked).
options.mono_fallback: Magenta ring→2px dashed white ring; nothing else changes.
options.source_inspiration: No Factorio source; a UI-craft idea (single reserved cursor hue). Magenta chosen because it is rarely used for status.

options.name: Field Notes Ochre
options.architecture: light / warm cream / ochre rules + pull-quotes (editorial register)

status.run: ▶ + word [RUNNING] + inverted row (static equivalent for reduced-motion)

color_independent_signals.selection_focus_unavailable: Selection = inverted fill; focus = outer dashed ring in focus_ring token; unavailable = dashed border + reason line.

options.hierarchy: Ochre = masthead rule, pull-quotes, links. Body ink on cream. Best for docs/marketing/editorial surfaces of Jaryo, not dense app chrome.
options.v1_change: Muted/unknown raised to pass AA on cream; OK/run no longer ochre.
options.tradeoff: Cream lowers ceiling contrast vs paper white; ochre as focus ring on cream is only ~5:1 — acceptable but near the limit on surface2.
options.source_inspiration: Interpretive of FTLO Field Notes paper dialect; not measured.

options.name: Dual Surface Day/Night
options.architecture: paired light+dark / one teal identity / MODE-CONSTANT mid-luminance status tints (3:1 on both grounds, words in text colour)

status.run: ▶ + word [RUNNING] + inverted row (static equivalent for reduced-motion)

color_independent_signals.selection_focus_unavailable: Selection = inverted fill; focus = outer dashed ring in focus_ring token; unavailable = dashed border + reason line.

options.hierarchy: Status glyph tints are the SAME in day and night (mid luminance passes 3:1 on both); labels use text colour. Teal identity is darkened for day and lightened for night.
options.v1_change: v1 checked only night text/bg (not night focus, border, status or selection); v2 computes both modes in full and picks status tints that work on both grounds.
options.tradeoff: The only system with coloured status glyphs: traffic-light semantics return, so glyph SHAPE + word remain mandatory; two matrices to maintain.
options.source_inspiration: No Factorio source; day/night pairing is a product need.

options.name: Hazard Stripe
options.architecture: dark / yellow hatch reserved for CONSEQUENTIAL chrome (review gate, destructive confirm) only

status.run: ▶ + word [RUNNING] + inverted row (static equivalent for reduced-motion)

color_independent_signals.selection_focus_unavailable: Selection = inverted fill; focus = outer dashed ring in focus_ring token; unavailable = dashed border + reason line.

options.hierarchy: Yellow/black diagonal hatch appears only on Review Gate headers, destructive confirms and irreversible-step markers. BLOCKED is NOT hazard: it is a grey panel with ✕ and a hard border so 'needs a human' (hazard) ≠ 'cannot proceed' (blocked).
options.v1_change: v1 let blocked be a solid hazard-yellow panel (conflated 'review needed' with 'blocked'); v2 separates them.
options.tradeoff: Overuse trains alarm blindness: hazard on idle chrome is forbidden. Hatch is visually loud at small sizes — min 24px band.
options.source_inspiration: Interpretive of Factorio hazard-concrete/yellow-black stripes (real in-game motif, not measured here).

options.name: Terminal Phosphor
options.architecture: dark / single-hue LUMINANCE LADDER (green) / amber cursor; hierarchy by brightness steps

status.run: ▶ + word [RUNNING] + inverted row (static equivalent for reduced-motion)

options.hierarchy: One hue, 4 brightness steps: text #B8FFC8 > accent #33FF66 > muted #4DBF6A > border #2F8A49. Selection inverts to bright green. Amber is the cursor only.
options.v1_change: v1 had text≈muted (#33FF66 vs #2ECC5A) — no hierarchy; v2 splits into an explicit ladder.
options.tradeoff: Green-on-black is the classic CRT look but long reading is tiring; offer F17.06 as the 'calm' alternative.
options.source_inspiration: Interpretive of CRT phosphor/terminal vibe from Louis's ASCII/TUI direction; not measured.
